SOURCE: Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B: Compressing Hybrid MoE LLMs. Bercovich, Abramovich, ... El-Yaniv (NVIDIA; ~70 authors). arXiv 2607.04371v2, 7 Jul 2026, preprint. File: ai-engineering/07-inference-engineering/sources/bercovich-2026-nemotron-labs-3-puzzle-75b.pdf

COVERAGE: All 81,246 chars of /tmp/potw-bercovich-2026-nemotron-labs-3-puzzle-75b.txt (1368 lines, 25 pages) read: main text, Tables 1-9, Appendices A-E (A.1 and A.2 read in two pieces). Only the NVIDIA et al. author-list references were skimmed. Figures were read via captions and plotted-number text only. I did not render the images.

IMPORTANT FRAMING: This is NOT early exit or layer skipping. It is static, hardware-aware structural pruning (Puzzle NAS plus distillation) of a hybrid Mamba/MoE/attention model, then quantization, then MTP speculative decoding. It fits 08-adaptive-inference best as a contrast to dynamic methods, or in the "stacking the gains" and MTP rows. It also fits notes/01 (throughput at matched user-speed) and 07 (Mamba state, KV at 1M context).

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Static compression gives about 2x server throughput at matched per-user speed on the decode-heavy workload.
 number: 2.03x (UT>=100), 2.14x (UT>=125), 2.12x (UT>=150) on 8K/64K. Only 1.60x, 1.69x, 1.79x on prefill-heavy 50K/2K.
 setup: 8xB200 node. Both models at NVFP4 weights, FP8 KV, FP16 Mamba SSM state with stochastic rounding. Single-step decoding, no MTP. Pareto sweep over TP in {1,2,4,8}, EP on/off, batch size up to memory. Super 120.7B/12.8B active vs Puzzle 75.3B/9.3B active.
 quote: "8K/64K ≥100 20,939 42,601 2.03×" and "single-step Puzzle-75B-A9B delivers between 1.6× and 2.14× the total throughput of Super" (Table 7, p.14; text p.13)
2. MTP stacks on top of compression and gives the biggest total gain. The abstract's "2x" is the single-step figure.
 number: Super+MTP 3.04x, Puzzle single-step 2.03x, Puzzle+MTP 4.63x (tokens/s), all relative to Super single-step.
 setup: 8K/64K, UT=100 tok/s, 8xB200 NVFP4, best draft length 3. Server throughput Super 20,939, Super+MTP 63,604, Puzzle 42,601, Puzzle+MTP 96,997 tok/s. Accuracy 71.93 (Super) vs 70.74 (Puzzle), average over the Table 3 suite.
 quote: "Puzzle-75B-A9B MTP best-DL 3 70.74 1.00 96,997 4.63×4.91×" (Table 4, p.10)
 NOTE, internal inconsistency: the prose says "2.18× ... 4.85× ... 3.57×" and "5.14×" for Puzzle+MTP, and Figure 1 uses a different baseline. Table 4 says 2.03x, 4.63x, 3.04x, and 4.91x for requests/min. Cite the table values and flag the prose.
3. Throughput should be adjusted for verbosity. Raw tokens/s misleads across models.
 number: Nano (30B/3.5B active) has 5.84x raw TPS but only 3.87x relative requests/min, because verbosity is 1.60 vs 1.00. Nano accuracy is 60.55%.
 setup: same as claim 2 (Table 4: 8K/64K, UT=100, 8xB200 NVFP4).
 quote: "Nano Single-step – 60.55 1.60 122,308 5.84×3.87×" and "deployment efficiency should be evaluated not only through token throughput, but also through effective request-level serving performance" (p.10)
4. Memory-bound long context: smaller weights free HBM for more concurrent 1M-token requests.
 number: 1M-context concurrency 1 to 8 on one H100 (80GB). Weights ~70GB (Super) vs ~44.5GB (Puzzle), both NVFP4. ~4GB KV per 1M request in both. Decode aggregate ~4x (Puzzle at bs=8 ~400 tok/s from 20.1ms ITL; Super at bs=1 ~94 tok/s from 10.7ms TPOT). Prefill of a 990K prompt ~1.2x faster.
 quote: "Super's weights occupy ∼70GB at NVFP4, and a single 1M-token request adds ∼4GB of KV cache; together these saturate the budget, so the parent's effective concurrency at 1M is 1." (App. C, p.21)
 caveat: NVFP4 is not native on Hopper. The authors use it anyway because HBM capacity is the binding constraint. The text calls the model "Super Turbo", an old name left in the appendix.
5. Continued training of the shared MTP head raises acceptance length (AL) and closes the NVFP4 gap.
 number: average AL 4.34 (BF16) / 4.31 (NVFP4) for Puzzle vs 3.45 / 3.31 for Super. That is about +25-30%.
 setup: SPEED-Bench "qualitative" split, draft length 7, 11 categories. Per category: coding 4.80, multilingual 5.31, roleplay 3.45 (lowest), writing 3.73.
 quote: "Average 3.45 (3.31) 4.34 (4.31)" (Table 5, p.10)
 mechanism: a shared MTP head is applied recursively. Teacher-forced training mismatches autoregressive drafting, because later draft steps condition on the head's own noisy hidden states. The fix is a training scheme that targets this mismatch (the paper does not give details). The Super head transferred to the compressed backbone with similar AL before extra training.
6. Iterative Puzzle (3 prune-then-heal rounds) beats one-shot pruning to the same final size, but only slightly.
 number: +0.57 average points (68.48 to 69.05). Largest gains: AA-LCR +2.2, GPQA +1.5. IFBench-Prompt -0.5, IFBench-Inst -0.2.
 setup: ten benchmarks, unweighted mean. Single run each, no variance reported.
 quote: "Iterative Puzzle improves the average by 0.57 points while preserving long-context performance" (Table 6, p.11)
 stages: MoE weights 75% with SSM state 75% (24B healing tokens), then MoE 60% (43.2B), then activated routed experts 50% (52.8B).
7. Accuracy retention.
 number: BF16 average over the Table 3 suite is close to Super. Examples: AIME25 89.7 vs 92.2, SWE-Bench 56.9 vs 59.5, GPQA no tools 78.6 vs 80.5, RULER-1M 92.2 vs 93.9, Arena-Hard-V2 68.6 vs 72.8 (largest gap).
 quote: "Arena-Hard-V2 69.0 72.6 68.6 72.8" (Table 3, p.9. Column order is Puzzle NVFP4, Super NVFP4, Puzzle BF16, Super BF16). Training progression: short-context KD recovers "over 97% of Nemotron-3-Super", and RL's effect was "small" (Fig. 4, p.11).
 verbosity: 132% of the parent right after pruning, back to 99% after recovery.
8. Hybrid-specific cost: Mamba SSM state pruning cuts decode cache IO.
 number: SSM state 128 to 96 channels gives a 1.2-1.3x SSM kernel speedup during decode at batch 8-512.
 quote: "for Nemotron-3-Super at batch sizes 64 and above, cache IO takes the majority of the Mamba layer decode time." (p.4)
 Contribution-based channel selection starts at 68.8 average accuracy vs 7.4 for random at the 75% setting (App. A.2, p.18). KD closes the gap.
9. Disaggregated prefill/decode allows a prefill-only smaller model, but the gain is small.
 number: +7% (FastPuzzleV1) and +5% (V2) prefill throughput. Common-average accuracy is 78.7 (V1) and 79.9 (V2) vs 79.9 baseline when decode stays on the full model. Using V1 for both prefill and decode drops it to 72.8.
 setup: 50K/1K, prefill top-k cut to 20% or 30% of Super's and embedding to 93% or 97%. Prefill and decode trained jointly (Star Elastic) so KV and SSM state transfer with no adapter.
 quote: "FastPuzzleV1 improves prefill throughput by 7%, and FastPuzzleV2 improves it by 5%" (App. B, p.20)
10. Final architecture.
 number: total params 62.4% of Super, active 73.1%. Routed expert intermediate size 1280-2688 (Super: 2688). Activated experts per token 4-18 (Super: 22). Mean active routed capacity 30.9%. 88 blocks: 40 Mamba, 40 MoE, 8 attention. Attention untouched.
 quote: "Active routed experts capacity (relative) 100% 8.7%–62.3% Mean 30.9%" (Table 1, p.6)
 Capacity is highly non-uniform across depth (Fig. 2).
11. H100 node results, FP8.
 number: 1.91x (50K/2K: 1,599 vs 838 tok/s) and 1.82x (8K/64K: 5,753 vs 3,163 tok/s) at UT=100.
 setup: 8xH100, FP8 weights and KV, FP32 Mamba state, no MTP. Not a primary target.
 quote: "Super Turbo 1.91× the total throughput of Super on 50K/2K (1,599 vs. 838 tok/s) and 1.82× on 8K/64K (5,753 vs. 3,163 tok/s)" (App. C, p.20)
12. Quantization policy (Table 2, p.8).
 FP8 and NVFP4 PTQ keep attention projections, the LM head, the whole MTP, the router (FP32) and the latent projections high precision. Mamba SSM state is FP32 on Hopper. On Blackwell it is FP16 with stochastic rounding (FP16 without SR loses accuracy, and FP16+SR is slower than FP32 on Hopper). Calibration: 256 samples (4K tokens each for FP8, 65K tokens each for NVFP4). FP8 and NVFP4 accuracy is slightly below BF16 (Table 3, Table 9).
13. Latent-dimension pruning was dropped.
 number: zero-shot LM loss at 768x768 latent: projection-based 1.050 vs Minitron 1.234 (teacher 0.937).
 setup: earlier Super checkpoint, no recovery.
 reason for dropping: it did not beat spending the same budget on channel and top-k pruning. NVFP4 kernels need latent dim to be a multiple of 512, so only 1024 to 512 is deployable.

LIMITS
- Not dynamic: no early exit or layer skipping. The architecture is fixed after training, and it needs about 120B+ tokens of distillation (24 + 43.2 + 52.8B across stages, plus long-context KD of up to 100B tokens at each of 128K and 512K) plus RL.
- MTP at best draft length uses synthetic or SPEED-Bench acceptance lengths for the Pareto overlay (App. C). The text still has a visible "TODO: drop in the headline MTP boost numbers ... from the latest report", so the MTP Pareto section is unfinished. Fig. 8 overlay boosts vs Super+MTP: +52.5% (UT100), +56.5% (UT150), +71.5% (UT200), +110.8% (UT300), +159.6% (UT400), on 8K/64K only.
- Accuracy cost is real: about 1.2 points on the average (71.93 vs 70.74). SWE-Bench is down 2.6 points and Arena-Hard 4 points. The authors say software-engineering ability degrades most.
- RL helped little. The ablation (Table 6) has no variance or seeds. No comparison against other compression methods is given besides 1-step Puzzle.
- Mamba pruning is uniform only because inference frameworks lack per-layer SSM sizes. Attention layers were not touched.
- The design target was 2x but the achieved single-step boost at UT=100 on the prefill-heavy workload is 1.60x (the text calls 1.6x the "design target", which conflicts with the intro's 2x).
- Vendor hardware and stack only (B200/H100, NVIDIA kernels). No independent replication. The 1M-context claim counts weights and KV only; Mamba state is "negligible" per the paper.
- Models are NVIDIA's own Nemotron family, and the benchmark set is the vendor's.

BUILDS ON
Puzzle (Bercovich et al., 2025, ICML) and its Puzzletron implementation (NVIDIA 2025); Extending Puzzle for MoE reasoning models / gpt-oss (Bercovich et al., 2026); Nemotron 3 Super and Nano (NVIDIA et al., 2026 / 2025); Minitron pruning (Muralidharan et al., 2024); speculative decoding (Leviathan et al., 2023); SPEED-Bench (Abramovich et al., 2026); Star Elastic (Taghibakhshi et al., 2026); LatentMoE (Elango et al., 2026); ASVD (Yuan et al., 2023); Model soups, weight averaging (Wortsman et al., 2022); Megatron-LM (Shoeybi et al., 2019).

CODE: None in the paper. The only formula worth keeping is the per-layer capacity metric (p.6): rho_l = (k_l * d_l) / (k_T * d_T), where k is activated experts and d is routed-expert intermediate size. Pareto method (p.13): sweep TP, EP and batch size, take the upper envelope of total TPS vs user TPS, and linearly interpolate at the UT threshold.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): accuracy vs relative request rate on 8xB200 NVFP4, normalized by verbosity. Shows that the 75B model with MTP matches Nano's request rate at near-Super accuracy.
- Fig 6 (p.13): Pareto frontiers of total vs user throughput for Super and Puzzle, with a boost-vs-UT panel (+60 to +79% on 50K/2K, +103 to +114% on 8K/64K). Good for teaching why throughput is quoted at a UT constraint.
- Fig 8 (p.20): MTP Pareto overlay. The MTP boost grows with the user-speed requirement.
- Fig 3 (p.10): MTP acceptance rate by draft token index.
- Fig 4 (p.11): training progression (accuracy as % of Super, with verbosity).
- Fig 5 (p.12): disaggregated prefill ablation bar chart.
- Fig 2 (p.7): per-layer MoE capacity.
- Table 4 is the best single exhibit for "stacking the gains" (compression x MTP) and for verbosity-adjusted throughput.

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean apart from some merged words and garbled table layouts (Table 6 and Figure 4 numbers are jumbled). I checked Table 3 against the column order in the header. No embedded instructions found. The text says "Super Turbo" in the appendices, an old model name. The prose figures (2.18x, 4.85x, 3.57x, 5.14x) contradict Table 4 (2.03x, 4.63x, 3.04x, 4.91x). Fig. 1's x-axis uses a different normalization. The abstract's "approximately 2x" is the single-step figure on 8K/64K, not the 1.6x prefill-heavy figure. The 4x figure on the H100 1M-context comparison compares different batch sizes (bs=8 vs bs=1).
